messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall — SEV2: elevated 504/502 from private inference gateway (us-west-2). Alert: gateway->model-backend timeouts spike. Root ts=2912340000
casey: seeing the same on dashboards — gateway 5xx rate ~15% for private vpc->backend path, started ~10m ago. Customers on dedicated/private show errors.
mira: noticed increased SYN_RECV / retransmits on the tcp metrics from gw -> transit-appliance. Could be asymmetric routing or DNAT/SNAT mismatch.
raj: i'm on it; pulling logs from the gateway. quick check: health probes to model nodes succeed from management plane.
alice: can we confirm if recent network change rolled last night? netops had a peering change scheduled. @netops-bot any config rollouts in us-west-2 in the last 12h?
netops-bot: Rollout log: transit-appliance:2026-03-14T23:12Z - applied DNAT rule update to support multi-tenant egress. Change-id: rn-9421. No rollback.
casey: interesting. traffic path: client -> inference-gateway (private) -> transit-appliance (DNAT/SNAT) -> model-backend. If DNAT applied asymmetrically it could break established connections and cause backend timeouts.
oncall-sre: taking incident lead. oncall handoff: @mira please be primary, @raj be secondary. I'll join for customer comms.
mira: thanks. First mitigation - divert new traffic to the backup egress region (us-east-1) for private customers with minimal routing policy change. That will reduce load on the affected path. Can netops run the route override?
raj: preparing the reroute. quick validation before cut: running curl to backend via transit appliance yields intermittent 504s: ``curl -sv http://10.10.12.45/health`` shows TCP handshake then 504 from gateway after 15s.
casey: capture from gateway shows lots of outbound SNAT ports in TIME_WAIT and some ICMP unreachable from transit box. suspect ephemeral port exhaustion combined with DNAT rewriting.
netops-bot: Observed NAT ephemeral-port usage: 92% used on transit-appliance-2 across us-west-2 pool.
alice: can we temporarily bump SNAT pool / spawn additional NAT appliance? that's faster than a config rollback.
mira: yes. raj, please spin a new transit appliance in the same AZ and attach to the SNAT pool; add it to the load balancing group. Also add a temporary security group rule to allow healthcheck traffic from gateway.
raj: spinning up t-transit-aux-03 now. command: ``aws ec2 run-instances --launch-template transit-aux --count 1 --region us-west-2``. attaching to nat-pool and registering to lb.
raj: registered. waiting for sync — health checks failing initially, prob because DNAT rules not synced.
casey: copy — check iptables/nat table on new appliance. maybe the change didn't propagate template.
raj: inspecting iptables: found the new appliance has default DNAT rule pointing to tenant overlay but missing SNAT fallback for gateway subnet. Adding rule: ``iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.100.0.0/16 -j MASQUERADE``
mira: after adding SNAT rule, I'm seeing failed sessions drop. Something else: some backends are returning RST when returning through a different egress. Could be security group on model node expecting traffic from specific source IP.
alice: are security groups locked down to the old transit IPs? check model-instances sg inbound rules.
raj: model-instance-sg inbound includes the transit subnet (10.200.0.0/22) but not the new transit-aux-03 IP. adding that now as temporary allow.
raj: patch applied. connectivity improved for ~30% of failed requests. gateway 5xx rate down to 6%.
mira: good. plan next: roll back the DNAT template change that netops-bot reported, or reconfigure DNAT to maintain source preservation for established flows. Which is faster?
netops-bot: DNAT change was applied via templated update. Rollback requires a deploy; alternative is hotfix to add source-preserve rule to NAT table.
casey: opt for hotfix to preserve source for existing sessions and then schedule a controlled rollback of the DNAT change to remove the incompatible rewrite.
oncall-sre: agree. while netops applies hotfix, we should notify affected customers and mark the incident page with mitigation steps. @alice draft a brief customer note.
alice: draft: "We're investigating elevated 5xx/timeout errors impacting private VPC inference in us-west-2. Traffic is being routed via a transit appliance update which caused asymmetric NAT. We're diverting new requests, adding capacity, and applying a NAT hotfix. We'll provide updates every 15 minutes." Will post to incident page and CS.
raj: applying hotfix script: ``/usr/local/bin/nat-hotfix.sh --preserve-source --reload`` — run on transit nodes. Patch logs: ``success: added SNAT preserve rule on transit-appliance-{1,2,aux-03}``.
mira: metrics now: gateway 5xx at 1.7%, latency back to normal for successful requests. No further customer escalations in the last 10m.
casey: leaving mitigation in place: extra transit aux + source-preserve hotfix + added sg entry. Next: schedule rollback of DNAT change to avoid future recurrence and add automation tests for ephemeral port saturation.
oncall-sre: runbook updates: add step to validate SNAT pool headroom before DNAT changes; add preflight healthcheck that simulates long-lived connections.
alice: posted customer message and updated incident page: https://redwood.incident/2912340000 (internal).
mira: closing timeline: outage window 2912340000 - 2912341500. moving to monitoring state. please add postmortem and assign owners: netops -> rollback DNAT change (owner: raj), infra -> NAT autoscale policy (owner: casey), prodeng -> add test (owner: mira).
oncall-sre: thanks all — handing back to normal ops. :thumbsup:
